countries.name: Canada
countries.introduction: Canada is one of the world's most sought-after study destinations, renowned for academic excellence, multicultural cities, and structured post-graduation work opportunities.
whyStudyHere: Globally recognized universities and applied polytechnic institutions
Structured Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility pathways
Safe, welcoming, and multicultural student communities
Comprehensive healthcare and student welfare frameworks
countries.educationSystem: Canadian higher education consists of research universities offering undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral degrees, alongside community colleges and institutes of technology providing specialized diplomas and applied degrees.
countries.admissionGuidance: Standard entry requires recognized academic credentials, English/French language proficiency (IELTS, TOEFL, PTE), academic transcripts, and letters of recommendation.
countries.visaGuidance: Study Permit applications require an official Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL), Letter of Acceptance (LOA) from a Designated Learning Institution (DLI), proof of financial support, and medical examination clearance.
countries.costInformation: Average undergraduate tuition ranges between CAD 18,000 to CAD 36,000 per year, with living expense requirements pegged to current IRCC standards.
countries.scholarshipInformation: Merit-based institutional entrance scholarships and international awards available based on prior academic performance.

faqs.question: Can international students work while studying in Canada?
faqs.answer: Eligible international students holding a valid study permit may work off-campus up to the government-stipulated hourly limits during academic semesters and full-time during scheduled breaks.

faqs.question: What is a Designated Learning Institution (DLI)?
faqs.answer: A DLI is a post-secondary institution approved by a provincial or territorial government to host international students.
